public_prompt: Decide whether an automated agent is hitting the login endpoint. The current line is: compare each day's failed-login total against the 30-day mean and flag any day beyond two standard deviations. Report whether automated activity is present and how you established it.
observable_resources: auth/per-minute.csv — 43,200 rows of failed-login counts at one-minute resolution over 30 days; mean 12.1, standard deviation 6.0
auth/daily-totals.csv — 30 rows; no day sits beyond two standard deviations of the 30-day mean
auth/autocorrelation.csv — the per-minute series shows a pronounced correlation peak at lag 900 minutes and again at 1800 and 2700
auth/source-addresses.csv — 4,100 distinct sources; none accounts for more than 0.4% of attempts
closure:threat-review-march — closed; records 'no automated activity detected' on the strength of the daily totals
closure:credential-strength-standard — closed; sets what a valid credential must contain; rests on the security standard, not on any finding about who is trying them

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer decomposes the per-minute series into periodic components, identifies the 900-minute period and its multiples as a regular non-human pattern, and states that daily aggregation destroys sub-daily structure. FAIL if the answer accepts 'no anomaly' from the daily totals, proposes per-address rate limits as the finding, or reports the correlation peaks without connecting them to a periodic component.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the daily-total framing reports no anomaly; the pattern lives entirely below the aggregation window.
